description: Flux (GitOps Toolkit) connector (read-only). Reads Flux Custom Resources directly from the Kubernetes API server — Kustomizations, HelmReleases, sources (GitRepository / OCIRepository / HelmRepository / Bucket), and image-automation objects (ImageRepository / ImagePolicy / ImageUpdateAutomation) — into the local index as a single `flux:resource` item type with a `kind` discriminator in metadata (external_id `<kind>/<namespace>/<name>`). Surfaces the `status.conditions` Ready health (ready_status True/False/Unknown + reason + message), `spec.suspend`, source `url`, kustomization `path`, and `last_applied_revision` / `last_attempted_revision`. Authenticates with a read-only Kubernetes ServiceAccount JWT sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; the API server base is supplied via the `flux.api_url` vault key. Flux has no central API and no SaaS host: the connector is always self-hosted, so the static manifest network list is intentionally empty — `phase3AddFluxMcp` parses the hostname from `flux.api_url` and extends the sandbox network list at spawn time (Grafana pattern). TLS note: Kubernetes API servers commonly present self-signed certificates that Bun's fetch rejects; v1 relies on `flux.api_url` pointing at a CA-trusted endpoint (a TLS-terminating ingress or `kubectl proxy`). Custom-CA / insecure-TLS handling is a deferred follow-up. Two HITL-gated write tools request a reconcile by annotating `reconcile.fluxcd.io/requestedAt` on the CR (PATCH): `flux_kustomization_reconcile` (HITL `flux.kustomization.reconcile`) and `flux_helmrelease_reconcile` (HITL `flux.helmrelease.reconcile`); both are async (verify via the next metadata sync) and require the ServiceAccount's `patch` RBAC verb on the target CR. `flux suspend`/`resume` remain deferred.
